record.original_question: In the hard-core/repulsive-gas context, Dobrushin's approach proves nonvanishing of the partition function Z first and then analyticity/convergence of log Z. Can this approach be extended so that it works without assuming hard-core self-repulsion?

evidence.quote: It is an interesting open question to know whether this approach can be made to work without the assumption of hard-core self-repulsion.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a lattice (or continuous) gas of polymers with activities $\{z_\gamma\}_{\gamma\in\Gamma}$ and a pairwise interaction encoded by a symmetric "compatibility" relation, with grand-canonical partition function
$$Z(\Lambda;z) \;=\; \sum_{\{\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_n\}\subset\Lambda} \prod_{i=1}^n z_{\gamma_i}\,\prod_{1\le i<j\le n} w(\gamma_i,\gamma_j),$$
where $w(\gamma,\gamma')\in[0,1]$ in the hard-core (purely repulsive) case is the indicator $\mathbf 1[\gamma\sim\gamma']$ of compatibility (so $w=0$ for incompatible polymers and $w=1$ otherwise). Dobrushin's inductive approach establishes, in this hard-core setting, the following two-step result for activities $z$ in an explicit polydisc $\mathcal D$:
(i) $Z(\Lambda;z)\ne 0$ for every finite $\Lambda$ and every $z\in\mathcal D$;
(ii) $\log Z(\Lambda;z)$ is analytic on $\mathcal D$ with absolutely and uniformly convergent cluster expansion.
The argument proceeds by induction on $|\Lambda|$, deriving (i) directly without recourse to power-series/cluster-expansion estimates, and then deducing (ii).

Question. Can Dobrushin's inductive approach be extended so as to prove the analogous nonvanishing and analyticity results for partition functions of polymer/lattice-gas systems whose pair interactions $w(\gamma,\gamma')$ are not assumed to enforce hard-core self-repulsion — for instance, soft-repulsive interactions $0\le w\le 1$, or more general (possibly complex-valued) Boltzmann weights — without assuming the hard-core constraint $w\in\{0,1\}$?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has extended Dobrushin-style inductive arguments beyond the strict hard-core case. Fernández–Procacci (2007) gave new bounds from an old approach for abstract polymer models, and later inductive proofs (e.g., the 2020 simple inductive proof of the Fernández–Procacci criterion) and follow-ups have established zero-freeness/cluster-expansion convergence in settings including soft-repulsive (0 ≤ w ≤ 1) and even complex-valued multi-body interactions. Thus the question is at least partially resolved in the affirmative for various classes beyond hard-core, although a fully general extension matching all features of Dobrushin's original argument is not uniformly stated as completely settled.

status_evidence.title: Cluster Expansion for Abstract Polymer Models. New Bounds from an Old Approach
status_evidence.snippet: Fernández–Procacci derive a new convergence criterion for abstract polymer models, improving Kotecký–Preiss and Dobrushin, via an inductive/tree-graph approach.
status_evidence.claim: Dobrushin-style inductive methods have been extended to give improved convergence/nonvanishing results in the abstract polymer setting beyond strict hard-core.

status_evidence.title: Abstract Polymer Gas: A Simple Inductive Proof of the Fernández–Procacci Criterion
status_evidence.snippet: Provides a Dobrushin-style inductive proof of the Fernández–Procacci convergence criterion for abstract polymer gas, including soft-repulsion regimes where only |1+x_e|≤1.
status_evidence.claim: The inductive 'no-cluster-expansion' approach extends to soft-repulsive interactions, not requiring hard-core self-repulsion.

status_evidence.title: Sufficient Conditions for Uniform Bounds in Abstract Polymer Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Sufficient conditions for zero-freeness of partition functions applicable to lattice gases with possibly complex-valued multi-body interactions.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizations beyond hard-core self-repulsion (including complex interactions) have been obtained.
